Are you excited by the intersection of people, data, and AI? Join us in shaping the future of People Analytics through modern analytics engineering, meaningful workforce insights, and data-driven decision-making.

About the role

Covering for the People Analytics and Data Strategy Engineer (“Data Analyst”), you will play a key role in taking the People & Culture data experience to the next level and support Urban Partners in reaching our ambitious goal of building the urban future, together. If you get energy from working for an internationally growing company and want to be part of making a difference, you may be our new team member!

In our People & Culture Team, we are a group of 16 colleagues covering 8 countries working together to support the business stakeholders in embodying our purpose and vision of making a difference for cities and people. You will have extensive interaction with team members and colleagues across the organization, promising exposure to a diverse range of expertise.

We can guarantee a dynamic environment with skilled colleagues, offering opportunities for learning, collaboration, and personal growth. You will be a part of a powerhouse of brilliant and caring people raising the bar for the industry. Your workplace will be at our headquarters located in Copenhagen, Nordhavn. As an international team, we regularly engage with colleagues across borders, fostering a global perspective and collaborative spirit.

In this role, you will be reporting to our Head of Reward, located in Copenhagen. The majority of this role will be carried out from our office with some flexibility.

This is a parental leave cover role on a fixed-term contract until end July 2027. Please note: we are unable to sponsor visa or work permit applications for this position. Applicants are responsible for ensuring they have the necessary right to work in Denmark prior to applying.

Key responsibilities

Over the past year, we've been experimenting with what People Analytics looks like when you treat it more like modern analytics engineering than traditional HR reporting. We have built our own analytics layer in Microsoft Fabric around an SCD2 master dataset of our employee population, with a Python semantic library on top. The setup supports workforce reporting used across senior management, the Board, financial planning, sustainability reporting and investor materials.

The role spans three closely connected areas: recurring workforce reporting, traditional People Analytics, and Reward. That means you'll work with everything from headcount and attrition analysis to the compensation review, pay transparency and ad hoc workforce questions. We've also designed the environment to work closely with modern AI assistants. LLMs are used to understand existing code, explore data, debug problems and help extend the analytical layer. We think this combination of structured data, reusable analytical logic and AI-assisted development represents an interesting direction for how People Analytics can work.

As Data Analyst, it is not simply a role where you “just” run existing reports and scripts. You'll inherit a working analytical system, learn how it fits together, keep it running reliably, and extend it when new business questions arise.

At the center of the setup is a master employee-history dataset combining the SCD2 states of our core HiBob data into one resolved timeline.

It allows us to reconstruct the workforce at historical points in time, covering approximately 20 years of employee history, with many core business rules already built into the data.

On top of this sits a Python semantic library with reusable building blocks for employee populations, joiners and leavers, turnover breakdowns, workforce bridges and much more.

Python notebooks use these components to produce recurring and ad hoc outputs including HTML reports, PowerPoint materials and Excel files.

The important part is not simply knowing how to run these tools. It is understanding the logic behind them, spotting when something does not look right, and knowing how far an answer needs to be taken before it creates business value.

These will be some of your key tasks

• Deliver key parts of the Reward cycle, including the 2027 salary review and gender pay gap and pay transparency reporting

• Support the data agenda for People & Culture, with the help of your People Lead

• Monitor data quality and investigate inconsistencies before they reach reporting.

• Run recurring workforce reporting covering headcount, FTE movement, joiners, leavers and attrition

• Support FP&A, Sustainability and Capital Formation with workforce data and analysis.

• Work on broader People Analytics questions, including workforce trends, organizational development and ad hoc analysis for senior stakeholders

• Answer new workforce questions as they arise

• Make careful extensions to the Python semantic library and reporting notebooks when needed

• Work with the BI team when source data or pipeline changes affect reporting

• Keep P&C's handling of employee data GDPR-compliant

• Build awareness and capabilities for the People & Culture team on data, analysis, and tools (e.g. Fabric, PowerBI, Excel)

Your experience & skills

• You're strong in Python and genuinely enjoy using it to solve problems

• You use LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot extensively to understand code, explore unfamiliar systems, debug problems and work faster

• You know that AI output still needs to be tested and verified

• You're comfortable learning things you haven't seen before

• You have a strong instinct for when data looks wrong

• You're comfortable taking ownership and working with senior stakeholders

• Ideally you have experience within remuneration or broader HR

• Ability to present data insights through clear and engaging visualizations

• Comfortable working with systems, ideally HR-related platforms

Your character

We hope you are a curious and continuous learner with a positive mindset. You take initiative, enjoy tackling challenges, and look for opportunities to improve the way things are done. Attention to detail is second nature, and you bring a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to complex problems. You're excited by how AI is transforming analytical work, while remaining focused on delivering accurate, useful, and high-quality outcomes.

Strong communication skills, diplomacy, and empathy are essential for building positive relationships across teams and functions. With a collaborative and service-minded approach, along with professional-level English skills, you thrive in a dynamic and international environment.

What we offer

Make a difference by helping create urban spaces and places that enrich people’s lives in the most sustainable way

Lead the industry with an innovator that is pioneering new approaches while raising standards and inspiring the industry

Learn and grow as part of a powerhouse of brilliant people where teamwork, feedback and different ways of thinking are at the core

Be your whole self in a purpose-driven culture with a strong sense of belonging, based on trust, celebration and caring for each other

Join us

If this opportunity interests you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as applications are reviewed and interviews conducted on an ongoing basis. Application deadline: 3 November.

We are happy to answer questions for more information, so please reach out to Joe Dias at jodi@urban.partners.

We look forward to hearing from you!

NORMAL has more than 1,000 stores across 14 countries. Twelve of these countries are supported from our warehouse in Hedensted, while the remaining two are supported from our warehouse in Horsens.

Our warehouse in Hedensted is an international workplace with around 60 different nationalities, and there is plenty to keep moving. We are looking for a Team Leader who can create the right conditions for people to succeed, while making sure our dayly picking operation runs smoothly.

You do not necessarily need a background in logistics to succeed in this role. What matters most is your ability to lead people, take responsibility and bring out the best in those around you.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Leading, supporting and developing a team of pickers and picking coordinators

• Creating clarity, structure and direction in the daily operation

• Motivating and guiding your team through feedback, coaching and everyday support

• Planning manpower needs and managing schedules

• Recruiting and onboarding the right people for the team

• Following up on picking performance, safety and compliance with our standards

• Identifying opportunities for improvement and turning good ideas into practical solutions

• Recognising and celebrating the difference your team makes to the operation

• Working closely with other warehouse departments to keep things running smoothly

• Acting as a role model: being a visible and involved leader in the daily operation, ready to step in when needed

**Who are you?

**You are the kind of leader who enjoys seeing other people succeed. You understand that strong results are created by strong teams, and you care about giving people the support, trust and space they need to do a good job.

You are approachable, organised and able to create structure without making things unnecessarily complicated. You communicate honestly and clearly, stay calm when priorities change and are comfortable making decisions when things get busy.

You do not have to know everything from day one. You are curious, open to learning and willing to develop both yourself and your team. You ask questions, listen to different perspectives and are not afraid to challenge the usual way of doing things when there is a smarter one.

At NORMAL, everyone has an important role to play. As a Team Leader, you will need to take ownership of your area, involve your team and follow things through. You give credit where it belongs, focus on the impact your team creates and help make their contribution visible.

You lead from the front and are not afraid to get involved when needed. At the same time, you know that leadership is not about having all the answers or being the loudest person in the room. It is about setting the team up to succeed, acting with integrity and creating results together.

And while we take the work seriously, we do not always take ourselves too seriously. There should be room for humour, spontaneity and a good laugh during the shift.

**We Also Expect That You

**

• Have experience leading a tea, ideally within picking, logistics or warehousing

• Have experience with a Warehouse Management System or similar tools, which would be an advantage

• Communicate confidently in English, both spoken and written

**Why NORMAL?

**At NORMAL, things move quickly, and there is rarely a long way from a good idea to action.

You will become part of an international operation with colleagues from around 60 different nationalities and a logistics centre that plays an important role in keeping our stores running across 12 countries.

You will have the opportunity to make a real difference, both to the daily operation and to the people around you. We believe in giving people responsibility and the freedom to find solutions, rather than expecting everything to be done in one particular way.

You will join a down-to-earth workplace where people help each other, share ideas and keep raising the bar. We do not expect every idea to work the first time. We expect people to try, learn, adjust and keep moving forward.

And if you can help create a team where people know what matters, feel trusted to do their job and enjoy coming to work, then you may be exactly the leader we are looking for.

**Practical information

**Location: Our logistics centre in Hedensted

Working hours: Full-time, 37 hours per week

Shift: Dayshift, 07.00-15.00

We hold interviews on an ongoing basis and hire when we find the right match.

If you have any questions about the role, please contact Picking Manager Ivan Donda at ivadon@normal.dk.

If you are ready to lead with energy, create direction and help your team succeed, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Greenland’s Firn Tipping Point - DTU Space
jobs.description:
Are you interested in turning natural phenomena into equations and code, and then applying them to big open questions in climate science? If so, we are looking for a PhD student with a background in physics and/or mathematics to help predict when Greenland’s porous near-surface firn layer, which currently stores much of the ice sheet’s meltwater, loses that capacity, and what that means for sea-level rise.

You will build models that combine physics, machine learning, and satellite data, and apply them to climate scenarios from the EU’s Destination Earth initiative. You will join a diverse and collaborative group at DTU Space and develop skills in scientific computing and machine learning that are valued in both research and industry. No prior experience in glaciology or climate science is needed; we will help you learn the field.

Responsibilities and qualifications
In the FirnTip project, you will develop a framework that predicts when and where Greenland’s firn stops being able to store meltwater, a possible climate tipping point. You will work closely with your supervisors at DTU Space as well as international partners. 

Your main tasks will be to:

• Identify which climate factors control when firn stops absorbing meltwater
• Combine satellite-derived firn density with firn models (data assimilation)
• Develop machine-learning models (e.g., graph neural networks) that obey physical conservation laws.
• Detect early-warning signals of tipping points in future climate scenarios
• Spend 3-6 months aboard visiting international partners, planned in collaboration with you
• Take part in teaching and knowledge-sharing as part of the DTU PhD program
To do well in the role, we think you need:

• A master’s degree in physics, mathematics or a field with a comparable mathematical foundation
• Experience writing scientific code, e.g., from your thesis or projects
• Good knowledge of at least one of: differential equations, numerical methods, statistics, or machine learning
• Good written and spoken English
Experience with glaciology, remote sensing, or machine learning is not required.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be conducted by Senior Researcher Sebastian B. Simonsen (DTU), Researcher Kirk M. Scanlan (DTU), and Senior Researcher Anja Rutishauser (GEUS) using common criteria for all applicants. Shortlisted applicants will have a structured interview, possibly including a short computational exercise. If you meet most, but not all, of the qualifications, please still apply. Let us know if you need any adjustments to the recruitment process. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The start date is February 1st or soon thereafter.

The position is a full-time position.

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Senior Scientist Sebastian B. Simonsen, ssim@dtu.dk. Questions about the project or the application are welcome. 

You can read more about our DTU Space cryosphere research at https://www.space.dtu.dk/english/research-divisions/geodesy-and-earth-observation/research-areas/cryosphere

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 29 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A one-page description of a computational or mathematical project you have done (e.g., your MSc thesis): the problem, your methods and your own contribution.
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates, irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background, are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

You will join the Cryosphere Research Group in the Geodesy and Earth Observation Division at DTU Space, Lyngby Campus. We use satellites, models and on-the-ground measurements to understand how ice sheets and glaciers are changing and what this means for sea level, in projects for ESA and the EU. Our group is international and collaborative, and we value curiosity, good supervision and a healthy work-life balance. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

**The Impact You'll Make

**At Danfoss Climate Solutions, we are committed to advancing sustainable and energy-efficient solutions that help our customers and communities thrive. As a Global Demand Planner (m/f/d), you will play a key role in ensuring our business has a reliable, data-driven view of future customer demand, enabling informed decisions across the value chain.

You will serve as a critical link between our commercial organization and supply chain teams, transforming data, market insights, and stakeholder input into robust demand forecasts. Your work will directly influence inventory levels, production planning, capacity utilization, and customer satisfaction.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys combining analytical thinking with business understanding. As part of our continued global growth, you will help shape best practices, drive continuous improvement, and create alignment across functions, while leveraging data and technology to make a measurable impact on our customers and business performance.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Own and continuously improve demand forecasts for assigned products, markets, or business areas by combining data analysis with commercial and market insights.

• Lead the monthly demand planning process and drive alignment with Sales, Marketing, Product Management, Supply Planning, and other key stakeholders.

• Analyze demand trends, forecast performance, and market developments to identify risks, opportunities, and actions that support better business decisions.

• Translate customer developments, product launches, phase-outs, and other business changes into accurate and actionable demand plans.

• Collaborate closely with Supply Planning to align demand and supply while supporting inventory, service, and operational targets.

• Contribute to the enhancement of demand planning processes, tools, automation, and digital capabilities to strengthen forecasting effectiveness.

**What We're Looking For

**

• Educational background in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Data Analytics, or a related field.

• Experience in demand planning, forecasting, S&OP, or a related supply chain discipline.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to transform data into meaningful business insights and recommendations.

• Experience working with Excel, ERP systems, planning tools, business intelligence platforms, or related technologies; knowledge of IBP is an advantage.

• Good understanding of forecasting principles and demand drivers, combined with the ability to communicate insights, challenge assumptions, and influence stakeholders across functions.

• A structured, proactive, and self-driven approach, combined with strong collaboration skills and professional English communication abilities.

**What You'll Get From Us

**

• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

• You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected, and valued for who they are.

• You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our **FAQ Page.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Process Modelling, Integration and Techno-Economic Analysis of Reversible Solid Oxide Electrolysis and biomethanation systems
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in process systems engineering at the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, Aarhus University, Denmark.

The successful applicant will contribute to a collaborative research and demonstration project focused on integrating reversible solid oxide electrolysis and fuel-cell operation with biogas production, biological methanation, and heat recovery. The research will combine process simulation, system integration, optimisation, and techno-economic analysis to evaluate flexible operation and support the scale-up of the technology.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two year position from 1st of February 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description
The successful applicant will contribute to a collaborative research and demonstration project focused on integrating reversible solid oxide electrolysis and fuel-cell operation with biogas production, biological methanation, and heat recovery. The advertised position has become available through an Energy Technology Development and Demonstration Programme (EUDP) Project from the Danish Energy Agency, called DyneMe. The project aims to demonstrate how a 300 kW second-generation Dynelectro electrolyser unit can boost biogas methane production from existing feedstock, maximise energy efficiency and provide grid-balancing capabilities through dynamic electrolyser load and when relevant fuel cell operation. The research will combine process simulation, system integration, optimisation, and techno-economic analysis to evaluate flexible operation. 

The main tasks include
• Developing process models, for all core unit operations, in Aspen Plus or comparable process-simulation software.
• Establishing mass and energy balances for electrolysis, fuel-cell operation, anaerobic digestion, biochemical methanation, biogas processing, steam production, and heat recovery.
• Evaluating the interaction between variable hydrogen production and biological hydrogen uptake.
• Identifying and evaluating heat-integration opportunities between the solid oxide system and the biogas facility.
• Simulating representative operating conditions, including part-load operation, hot standby, and SOEC and SOFC operating modes.
• Combining process-model results with time-series or dispatch models to assess operation under variable electricity prices, renewable-electricity availability, biogas production, and heat demand.
• Conducting techno-economic, sensitivity, and uncertainty analyses.
• Participating in regular project meetings and present the modeling activities.
Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering, energy engineering, biochemical engineering or similar.

The successful candidate is expected to have 
• A strong background in process modelling, thermodynamics, mass and energy balances, and chemical or energy-process design.
• Extensive experience with Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, or comparable process-simulation software.
• Experience in developing, analysing and validating models of chemical, biochemical, electrochemical, or energy-conversion processes.
• Experience with process integration, including pinch analysis and heat exchanger network design.
• Documented experience with techno-economic analysis, including sensitivity and uncertainty analysis.
• Experience with quantitative data analysis and a relevant programming or numerical-computing environment, such as Python or MATLAB.
• The ability to work independently, structure a complex modelling problem, document assumptions, and deliver results according to project deadlines.
• Documented ability to have scientific results of high quality published in peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and spoken English.
• Good communication and collaboration skills and an interest in working in an interdisciplinary project involving both academic and industrial partners.
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage
• Dynamic process simulations
• Mathematical optimisation 
• Development of surrogate models
• Electrolysis, fuel cells, hydrogen production or other electrochemical processes
• Biogas production, anaerobic digestion, biological methanation
Who we are
Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering (BCE) was established on January 1, 2021 in connection with Aarhus University’s reorganization of the engineering area. The department employs around 260 people and is responsible for research and education within the department’s scientific areas. We educate both Bachelors and Masters of Science in Engineering and around 825 students are enrolled in our study programs. Furthermore, we also offer an ambitious PhD program. Our PhD students have high academic ambitions and deliver high-quality results for both the private and the public sectors.

At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, focus is on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering, and more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food. 
BCE has strong research sections in Chemical Process Engineering and Bioprocess Engineering, among others. The successful candidate will be working within the Microbial Conversion Technologies and the Sustainable Process Systems Engineering groups.

What we offer 
• the opportunity to be part of a team developing novel technologies for sustainable fuels and make a high impact in solving climate change issues. 
• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment, software and databases 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Gustav Wieds Vej DK-8000, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Assoc. Prof. Michael Vedel Wegener Kofoed, mvk@bce.au.dk, +4593521051.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 27th of November.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

DHL Global Forwarding (Denmark) is looking for an experienced Air Freight Pricing Specialist

At DHL Global Forwarding, competitive air freight solutions are about more than offering the lowest price. They are about understanding the market, making commercially sound decisions and finding the right balance between cost, capacity, service quality and customer expectations.

As our new Air Freight Pricing Specialist, you will play a central role in supporting the commercial performance of our air freight product. You will be responsible for developing competitive pricing solutions, supporting tenders and ensuring that our pricing decisions reflect both market conditions and business objectives.

Working closely with airlines, customers and colleagues across Sales, Operations and our international network, you will translate market insights and commercial requirements into pricing solutions that strengthen our competitiveness.

This is a role for someone who understands the dynamics of international air freight, enjoys working with commercial data and negotiations, and takes ownership of delivering accurate and competitive solutions – often within tight deadlines.

You will become part of our Air Freight pricing organization, where market knowledge, commercial judgement and collaboration are essential to success.

Your key responsibilities in the role will be to:

• prepare and deliver competitive air freight quotations, RFQs and tenders, ensuring accurate pricing, timely submissions and alignment with customer requirements.

• support the implementation of our air freight pricing strategy, balancing commercial objectives, profitability and company guidelines.

• negotiate competitive rates and service conditions with airlines and other suppliers, considering cost, capacity, service quality and transit time requirements.

• build and maintain strong relationships with airline partners, customers and internal stakeholders, ensuring effective collaboration on commercial opportunities and high-priority tenders.

• monitor air freight market developments, capacity, rates and trade lane opportunities, and analyze airline performance to support informed pricing decisions.

• maintain accurate tariffs, pricing databases and supporting tools, while identifying opportunities to improve pricing processes, efficiency and competitiveness.

• share knowledge and provide guidance to colleagues on complex pricing matters, contributing to continuous improvement and professional development within the team.

We are looking for someone, who:

• combines a strong operational understanding with the ability to see opportunities for improvement and development.

• enjoys leading change and understands that successful implementation requires both clear direction and involvement of the people affected.

• works in a structured and analytical manner, using data and operational insights to support decisions.

• takes ownership of challenges and follows improvement initiatives through to completion.

• can balance operational efficiency, quality, compliance and customer expectations.

• communicates clearly and confidently with stakeholders at different organizational levels.

• can influence and create alignment across teams and functions, even without direct managerial authority.

• enjoys developing colleagues, sharing knowledge and building a culture of continuous improvement.

• is comfortable working in an international organization where local priorities and global standards must work together.

We expect you to have:

• have more than 4 years of relevant professional experience, preferably within air freight forwarding, pricing or airline-related commercial activities.

• have a solid understanding of air freight products, market dynamics and commercial pricing principles.

• have experience working with quotations, RFQs, tenders or commercial negotiations.

• be comfortable analysing pricing information, market data and commercial performance.

• have strong Microsoft Excel skills and experience working with pricing tools or databases.

• have experience collaborating with airlines, suppliers or other commercial stakeholders.

• hold a Bachelor's degree or have equivalent relevant experience and qualifications.

• be fluent in English, both verbally and in writing. Danish language skills are considered an advantage.

And from us, you can expect:

• a specialist role with direct influence on the commercial competitiveness of our air freight product.

• the opportunity to work with international airline partners and global freight forwarding networks.

• a position in a global organization with extensive professional and personal development opportunities.

• close collaboration with experienced colleagues across Sales, Operations and our international organization.

• a working environment where commercial judgement, collaboration and responsibility are valued.

• being part of THE logistics company for the world.

• pension, health insurance, internal development opportunities and more.

Workplace: DHL Global Forwarding, Hedegaardsvej 88, 2300 Copenhagen S – and as part of the job, you will have some traveling, mostly domestically, but as well internationally.

Working hours: The position is a full-time position

The compensation package:

The base salary is determined by your qualifications and competencies. The position is graded and sit within a predefined payband. Besides the base salary you will have – just to mentioned a few of the benefits - a pension scheme, bonus scheme, 25+5 vacation days per year, and a “Fritvalgskonto” (a “saving account” equal to 10% of your annual salary) paid out in December.

How to apply:

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, and as we recruit as soon as the right person is found, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Your application should include your CV and a short description of why you see yourself as a strong match for the role.

If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out to Head of Growth Michael Schønning at michael.schonning@dhl.com.

Location: European hubs (flexible)

**Role Summary

**We are seeking a commercially minded, market-facing leader to drive the growth and adoption of our portfolio of digitally enabled and AI-enhanced forensic solutions across Europe, with extension into APAC. Our Integrity & Compliance solution is a flagship offering within this portfolio and will feature prominently — but the role spans the wider set of technology-led forensic solutions we need to commercialise.

The central purpose of the role is market activation: helping country and regional Forensics teams move from traditional, manual delivery to modern, technology-led ways of serving clients — and, in doing so, unlocking new revenue. The successful candidate will partner with local leaders to build go-to-market approaches, shape and win opportunities, and accelerate the adoption of new solutions in their markets.

This is a commercial and go-to-market role first. The successful candidate does not need deep, hands-on technical expertise, but must be fluent enough in forensic technology and AI to speak about it credibly, translate capability into client value, and help territories both commercialise and deliver these solutions.

**Key Responsibilities

****Strategic Market Development

**

• Drive the execution of the European (and, by extension, APAC) growth strategy for our digitally enabled forensic solutions, aligned to global priorities and regional targets.

• Identify market opportunities, emerging regulatory trends and client needs to expand the solution portfolio across countries.

• Partner with Regional and Country Forensics leaders to build market plans, go-to-market approaches and priority pursuits.

• Develop practical playbooks, propositions, case studies and market materials that help countries accelerate revenue and client penetration.

• Track market performance and pipeline to focus effort where growth potential is greatest.

**Driving Adoption & Commercial Enablement

**

• Lead the shift from manual, traditional delivery to technology-led delivery — acting as the catalyst for behaviour change across local teams.

• Equip country leaders and teams to confidently position, sell and scale technology-enabled forensic solutions.

• Act as a trusted commercial advisor to country leaders establishing or expanding these offerings.

• Facilitate knowledge sharing and leading practices across Europe and APAC to build commercial momentum and consistency.

• Help local leaders understand — at the right level — how technology, analytics and AI translate into client value and competitive advantage.

**Client Engagement & Commercial Leadership

**

• Support strategic pursuits and priority opportunities across the forensic solution portfolio, including Integrity & Compliance, investigations, monitoring, forensic data analytics, eDiscovery, third-party and regulatory risk, and AI-enabled solutions.

• Help countries shape complex proposals and solution approaches for priority opportunities.

• Identify cross-border opportunities and bring global capability to bear to win and deliver client work.

• Drive pipeline development and revenue growth across priority markets.

**Market Presence & Thought Leadership

**

• Represent the firm at client forums, industry events and internal leadership meetings.

• Champion the firm's perspective on technology-enabled, AI-enhanced forensic solutions.

• Develop market insights and commercial materials that support business development and portfolio growth.

• Deliver compelling presentations and demos for country leaders, practitioners and clients.

**Stakeholder Management

**

• Build strong relationships with Regional and Country Forensics leaders to advance growth objectives.

• Influence senior stakeholders across geographies to back adoption and growth initiatives.

• Foster cross-region collaboration to share resources, opportunities and leading practices.

**Qualifications

****Required

**

• Demonstrated success in commercialising services and driving revenue growth within a professional services environment — ideally new or technology-enabled offerings.

• Proven ability to drive change and adoption across distributed, matrixed teams.

• Strong client network and market-facing relationships that can be leveraged.

• Excellent stakeholder management, influencing and executive-level communication skills.

• Sufficient fluency in forensic technology and AI to speak credibly and connect capability to client value — deep hands-on technical expertise is not required.

• 10–15 years' experience within Forensics, Compliance, Regulatory Risk, Financial Crime, Investigations or related Forensic & Integrity services.

**Preferred

**

• Experience across European and APAC markets.

• Knowledge of Integrity & Compliance disciplines (ABC, third-party risk, monitoring, investigations, ethics programmes).

• Awareness of advanced analytics and AI applications relevant to forensics and regulatory risk.

• Multilingual capabilities (English plus another major European language).

**Success Metrics

**

• Revenue growth and pipeline expansion across the forensic solution portfolio in Europe and APAC.

• Measurable shift from manual/traditional to technology-led delivery in priority markets measured through adoption of technology.

• Increased capability and participation of country teams in selling and delivering technology-enabled solutions.

• Growth in cross-border and multi-country engagements.

• Market-facing assets and thought leadership that support commercial growth.

**Working Model

**

• Hybrid across European hubs; travel 30–50% for client meetings, country activation and leadership forums.

Reports to [confirm exact global reporting line]; close collaboration with Global, Regional and Country Forensics leadership.

**EY | Building a better working world

**EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

Join a team of fintech heroes! 🚀

Performativ is changing the way investment advisors and financial institutions operate. We are building a modern platform for portfolio management, reporting, compliance, trading, and client engagement, replacing fragmented systems, manual workflows, and technology built for another era.

Our customers include wealth managers, asset managers, family offices, and financial institutions across Europe and beyond. We are on an ambitious scaling journey, supported by leading global venture capital investors, and are working to become the platform on which modern wealth management runs.

You can read more about our product at performativ.com.

As our new Software Engineer, Reporting & Fee Management 📈

You will help build the products our customers use to communicate investment results and charge their clients.

Reporting and fee management look simple from the outside, but every wealth manager has its own data, calculations, presentation requirements, commercial agreements, and operating processes. Joining Performativ should not require customers to abandon what makes their business work.

Our direction is to turn these differences into flexible, reusable platform capabilities. This includes a new reporting workbench and AI-assisted experiences that allow users to configure, generate, and publish reports and fee arrangements safely themselves.

• 
You will build reporting and fee-management capabilities that turn complex portfolio data and customer requirements into accurate, understandable outputs.

• 
You will work closely with users and customer-facing colleagues to understand real workflows, challenge assumptions, and distinguish reusable product needs from one-off requests.

• 
You will help develop self-service configuration and AI-assisted workflows, with clear validation, permissions, review steps, and safeguards for untrusted input.

• 
You will investigate issues across data, calculations, configuration, and presentation, then deliver permanent solutions that are observable, testable, and safe to deploy.

• 
You will direct AI agents to produce much of the implementation, review their decisions and output critically, and leave systems in a state that teammates can understand and extend.

You should bring solid software-engineering judgment and an interest in developing product and financial-domain understanding. Experience with investment reporting, fee calculations, portfolio data, document generation, configurable workflows, or financial software would be valuable, but deep experience with our exact technology stack is not required.

We value your passion 🔥

At Performativ, we are builders first. We have ambitious goals and value the time, judgment, and effort people put into their work. You will be trusted to make your mark and help shape how we solve difficult problems.

We do not divide the platform into personal territories. People develop deeper context in different areas, but we solve problems as a team. We expect people to lead when appropriate, follow through on what they take on, contribute to the work of others, and help teammates succeed.

AI increases our delivery speed, but it does not reduce our engineering standard or our accountability for the result. You must be able to recognise incorrect assumptions, missing edge cases, weak product decisions, and unsafe production behaviour.

This role is based in Copenhagen. We work together primarily from our city-centre office, with flexibility to work from home when it makes sense. You should already be based in Copenhagen or be ready to relocate.

What we can offer you 🌱

• 
The opportunity to build products used directly by wealth managers and their clients.

• 
Difficult product and engineering problems involving financial data, calculations, configuration, document generation, and AI-assisted workflows.

• 
A central role in making complex reporting and fee management genuinely self-service.

• 
An ambitious, collaborative team with experience from leading technology companies, consultancies, and financial institutions.

• 
Strong opportunities for professional development as Performativ grows.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

Want to shape how millions of holidaymakers discover their next getaway? At Awaze, you'll take the lead on one of the industry's largest OTA network, building strong commercial partnerships, unlocking new growth opportunities and helping us reach even more guests across Europe.

**Your mission

**As our new Head of 3rd Party Partnerships, your mission is to maximise the performance of Awaze's third-party distribution channels, from OTAs and travel agency chains to strategic digital partners.

You'll take ownership of an established partner network, with the freedom to shape its future, optimise channel performance and negotiate agreements that drive commercial growth. As a key representative of Awaze in the industry, you'll turn market insights into opportunities, working closely with Commercial, Product, Marketing and leadership teams to deliver measurable results.

**What You'll Be Doing

**

• Own and develop relationships with OTAs, travel agency chains and strategic distribution partners, driving channel performance and revenue growth.

• Identify, negotiate and secure high-value commercial agreements with new and existing partners, managing relationships from onboarding to long-term development.

• Analyse channel performance, KPIs and market trends to uncover growth opportunities and guide commercial decisions.

• Collaborate with Product, Tech, Marketing, Pricing and regional teams to optimise distribution, improve partner integrations and support platform transitions.

• Drive joint marketing initiatives and ensure partners have the tools, data and support needed to succeed.

• Represent Awaze at industry events, conferences and partner meetings, building our network and strengthening our market position.

**Who We're Looking For

**You'll thrive in this role if you're commercially driven, enjoy building relationships and know how to turn data and market insights into results. You're a confident negotiator who can move comfortably between strategic discussions, technical conversations and hands-on operational tasks.

**We're Looking For Someone Who Brings

**

• Strong experience in managing and optimising third-party distribution channels, ideally within travel or hospitality.

• Proven commercial and negotiation skills, with a track record of securing valuable partnerships and driving revenue growth.

• An analytical mindset, using performance data and market insights to make informed decisions.

• Technical understanding of distribution platforms and integrations, including Message API, multi-rate and similar solutions.

• Excellent relationship-building, communication and networking skills, with confidence representing Awaze externally.

• A proactive, collaborative approach, excellent written and spoken English, and curiosity about how AI can improve ways of working.

It will be a bonus if you have experience with major OTA platforms and their commercial dynamics, or speak German and/or Danish.

**How You'll Make An Impact

**

• Maximise revenue and performance across our established third-party distribution network.

• Expand our reach by identifying new strategic partners and securing stronger commercial agreements.

• Improve channel optimisation through data-driven decisions, technical improvements and cross-functional collaboration.

• Bring valuable market intelligence into Awaze to influence commercial and product strategies.

• Strengthen Awaze's industry presence and build long-lasting partnerships that support sustainable growth.

You’ll be part of an international company that invests in the future, and join a dynamic, fast-paced department with skilled and committed colleagues who support each other.

We’re a People-first Business - And We Know That Our Success Starts With Our Teams. Here’s a Glimpse Of What You’ll Enjoy

• Flexible hybrid working – with the autonomy to work how you work best

With more than 110,000 properties across Europe, we are the largest managed vacation rentals business in the region. Our ambition is not only to be the biggest, but the best provider of holiday homes in Europe.

We will keep strengthening our relationships with guests and homeowners, continuously improving the way we work, and delivering strong performance. About Linkfire and where we're heading

Linkfire is the marketing platform the music industry uses to connect fans with the music they love. Trusted by major labels including Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment and BMG, as well as thousands of independent artists, labels, and podcasters, our smart links, bio links, and landing pages power music discovery and engagement every day.

We recently launched Artist Workspaces, giving every artist their own home on Linkfire and the foundation for a new generation of fan intelligence features. Our next chapter is about helping artists and their teams really know their fans: who they are, what they care about and how to reach them again. That means selling more tickets and more merch, and building fan relationships that last well beyond release week.

We have a packed roadmap heading into 2027, and it's vital that our customers know about the features we're shipping and see the value in them. That's where you come in.

The role

We're back in growth mode and rebuilding marketing, starting with this role. For now you'll operate as our solo in-house marketer, owning product marketing end to end. You'll report to the Director of Product and work closely with our product managers and commercial team.

The first job is clear: get our existing customers using what we've built, and turn their results into stories that help us sell to others.

You'll start with our owned channels (email, in-app, our website and socials) and our artist and label relations managers. You'll also have budget to get in front of customers, through industry events, visits to key clients and getting our message out more widely. If webinars or other new channels make sense, you can lead building them.

This isn't a performance marketing role. We expect to add performance and acquisition marketing when the time is right, as a dedicated function with its own resources, not an extra job on top of this one.

As marketing grows, there's a path to building and leading a team covering brand and identity, website, socials, and the onboarding journeys that convert new customers and keep existing ones.

What you will do

• Own the go-to-market for every feature and product launch: the narrative, who hears what and when, and the comms, assets and sends.

• Drive adoption and measure it, so we know which campaigns move usage and which don't.

• Identify customers getting value from the product, and turn their stories into case studies, testimonials, and content snippets our commercial team can use in sales conversations.

• Run our owned channels, from email and in-app to the website and socials, and own the tooling behind them.

• Represent Linkfire at industry events and in meetings with key customers.

What we are looking for

You might be a product marketer, a customer or lifecycle marketer, or a generalist who has run marketing on your own. The title matters less to us than what you've done.

• Several years in B2B or SaaS marketing, with a track record of launching features to existing customers and getting them used.

• Positioning instincts. You can work out who a feature is for, what problem it solves and why it matters, then build the launch around that.

• Hands-on experience with customer messaging tools such as Intercom, including segmentation and automation.

• Clear, persuasive writing in English. You can turn a technical feature into something a busy label marketer or artist manager will actually read.

• An eye for design and comfort creating content yourself. You’ll produce visuals and short videos for launches, working with our designer on the bigger pieces.

• Comfort with data. You set up tracking, read the results and change what you do because of them.

• An eye for a good customer story, and the persistence to get it signed off and published.

• You already use AI in your daily work and have opinions about where it helps and where it gets in the way.

Nice to have

• Knowledge of the music industry, or another creator or entertainment market.

• An interest in how fan and customer data gets captured and used, whether from working with CRM or CDP tools or just being curious about it.

• Experience working asynchronously in a distributed team.

Location

We’d love you to be based in Copenhagen or elsewhere in Denmark. We’re a distributed company and plenty of our colleagues are fully remote, but we have a cosy office on Rentemestervej where many of us visit a couple of days a week. This helps us stay in sync and we’d like it if you can join us.

English is our working language, and all our customer comms are in English too, so you don’t need to speak Danish.

How to apply

Along with your CV, tell us about a feature launch you ran: what you did, and what happened to adoption afterwards. A couple of paragraphs is plenty.

Why join Linkfire

• Real ownership from day one. How we launch and talk to customers is yours to shape.

• Be part of what's next. We're changing what Linkfire offers, and you'll help tell that story.

• A product people already use. Millions of fans interact with our customers' landing pages every day, so there's real usage to build on.

• Flexible, distributed team. Colleagues across several countries, a Copenhagen office for those who want to be together, and working hours that fit around your life.

• Benefits. Six weeks’ paid holiday and a 4% company pension contribution.
